title: Checks for code that raises Exception or BaseException directly.
summary: Handling such exceptions requires the use of except Exception or except BaseException. These will capture almost _any_ raised exception, including failed assertions, division by zero, and more. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.236.

title: Checks for long exception messages that are not defined in the exception class itself.
summary: By formatting an exception message at the raise site, the exception class becomes less reusable, and may now raise inconsistent messages depending on where it is raised. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.236.
message_templates: Avoid specifying long messages outside the exception class

title: Checks for type checks that do not raise TypeError.
summary: The Python documentation states that TypeError should be raised upon encountering an inappropriate type. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.230.

title: Checks for exceptions that are re-raised without specifying the cause via the from keyword.
summary: The from keyword sets the __cause__ attribute of the exception, which stores the "cause" of the exception. The availability of an exception "cause" is useful for debugging. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops, and removed it.
message_templates: Use `raise from` to specify exception cause

title: Checks for needless exception names in raise statements.
summary: It's redundant to specify the exception name in a raise statement if the exception is being re-raised. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.231.

title: Checks for immediate uses of raise within exception handlers.
summary: Capturing an exception, only to immediately reraise it, has no effect. Instead, remove the error-handling code and let the exception propagate upwards without the unnecessary try-except block. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in 0.7.0.
message_templates: Remove exception handler; error is immediately re-raised

title: Checks for return statements in try blocks.
summary: The try-except statement has an else clause for code that should run _only_ if no exceptions were raised. Returns in try blocks may exhibit confusing or unwanted behavior, such as being overridden by control flow in except and finally blocks, or unintentionally suppressing an exception. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.229.
message_templates: Consider moving this statement to an `else` block

title: Checks for raise statements within try blocks.
summary: The only raises caught are those that throw exceptions caught by the try statement itself. Raising and catching exceptions within the same try block is redundant, as the code can be refactored to avoid the try block entirely. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.233.

title: Checks for uses of logging.error instead of logging.exception when logging an exception.
summary: logging.exception logs the exception and the traceback, while logging.error only logs the exception. The former is more appropriate when logging an exception, as the traceback is often useful for debugging. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.236.

title: Checks for excessive logging of exception objects.
summary: When logging exceptions via logging.exception, the exception object is logged automatically. Including the exception object in the log message is redundant and can lead to excessive logging. Ruff takes this rule from tryceratops and made it stable in v0.0.250.
message_templates: Redundant exception object included in `logging.exception` call

title: Check that expression is not implicitly true in boolean context.
summary: Warn when the type of an expression in a boolean context does not implement __bool__ or __len__. Unless one of these is implemented by a subtype, the expression will always be considered true, and there may be a bug in the condition. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code truthy-bool to enable it.

title: Check that function isn't used in boolean context.
summary: Functions will always evaluate to true in boolean contexts. mypy enables this error code by default.

title: Check that iterable is not implicitly true in boolean context.
summary: Generate an error if a value of type Iterable is used as a boolean condition, since Iterable does not implement __len__ or __bool__. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code truthy-iterable to enable it.
